headline: Phillies host Braves tonight after finale loss in Arizona
recap: Andrew Painter delivered his best start of the season Wednesday in Arizona, working seven scoreless innings with six strikeouts and no walks while allowing just two hits, but the Phillies could not deliver enough offense behind him and he left with a no-decision. The game stayed scoreless until the bottom of the eighth, when James McCann hit a solo home run off reliever Jonathan Bowlan (2-2) for the Diamondbacks' only run of the game; Jonathan Loáisiga picked up the win and Juan Morillo closed it out for the save in a 1-0 Arizona victory. Philadelphia managed only three hits: two from Bryan De La Cruz, including a double, and one from Bryce Harper, who also drew two walks. The rest of the lineup was held hitless.
The loss leaves the Phillies at 79-61, second in the NL East, four games behind the division-leading Braves, and working on a one-game losing streak.

After Thursday's scheduled off day, the Phillies open a four-game series at home against Atlanta tonight at Citizens Bank Park, with first pitch at 6:40 PM ET. Cristopher Sánchez starts for Philadelphia opposite the Braves' Chris Sale. DraftKings has the Phillies as slight moneyline favorites at -118, with Atlanta at -102.
